text:
The Maple Leafs have spent the week answering questions: about Auston Matthews and the trade rumours that won't stop, about William Nylander's public disagreement with his drop to the second power-play unit ("I didn't agree with it," as TSN's headline put it), about how Jim Hiller uses Gavin McKenna. On Friday afternoon in Boston, the answer came from the blue line. Morgan Rielly scored twice, the second his 100th career goal, and Toronto won 3-1 at TD Garden.

Neither of Rielly's goals came from anywhere dangerous. The first, at 16:53 of the first period, was a wrist shot our model gave a 1% chance; it erased Casey Mittelstadt's power-play goal from earlier in the period. The second, late in the second, had a 3% chance and moved Toronto's win probability from 48% to 71%. The Leafs Nation noted he is the fourth defenceman in franchise history to reach 100 goals with the club.

Colton Sissons, back in the lineup, made it 3-1 at 7:24 of the third with the best chance of Toronto's afternoon, a 14% snap shot set up by McKenna. After that it was Anthony Stolarz's game. Boston owned the third period, 1.22 expected goals to Toronto's 0.65, and outshot the Leafs 29-18 overall, but Stolarz stopped 28 of 29 and saved 1.3 goals more than those shots deserved.

On chances this was close to even: 2.28 expected goals for Boston, 2.07 for Toronto, and the Bruins deserved to win 56% of the replays of every shot. Jeremy Swayman, already under scrutiny for a rough stretch, allowed three on 18 shots. The worse news for Boston came off the scoresheet: David Pastrnak left with a lower-body injury, per Daily Faceoff. Toronto lost Chris Tanev the same way. Both teams will be waiting on those updates more than they'll be thinking about the score.
headline: Rielly's 100th steadies the Leafs in Boston
